judged_text: In createEvent, when no destinationCalendar entry matches the passed credentialId, the event silently falls back to calendarId "primary", whereas the old code used the stored destinationCalendar.externalId. Legacy destination rows without a credentialId (the case EventManager's else-branch still serves by calling createEvent(c, event) with no externalId) now create every Google event on the organizer's primary calendar instead of the user's selected destination calendar — bookings silently land in the wrong calendar with no error surfaced to the user.

Legacy destination rows without a credentialId (the case EventManager's else-branch still serves by calling createEvent(c, event) with no externalId) now create every Google event on the organizer's primary calendar instead of the user's selected destination calendar — bookings silently land in the wrong calendar with no error surfaced to the user.

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, the calendarId is now chosen via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, and falls back to `"primary"` when no match is found (`calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`). Under `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the else-branch for destinations without `credentialId` still calls `createEvent(c, event)` for each matching credential type, but those `DestinationCalendar` entries may not have `credentialId` set, so the `.find(...)` returns undefined and Google inserts into the organizer's primary calendar. Previously Google used `destinationCalendar.externalId` directly when present, so this change can silently route events to the wrong calendar for legacy destinations.
